questions.q: What problem does using a standardized questionnaire like SIG or CAIQ solve compared to a custom questionnaire built from scratch for every vendor?
options: It guarantees a vendor cannot have any security weaknesses
It makes answers comparable across vendors and lets vendors reuse work they've already done for other customers, reducing assessment fatigue on both sides
It eliminates the need for any contractual security requirements
It is required by law in every jurisdiction before any vendor contract can be signed
questions.explain: A bespoke questionnaire makes every vendor's answers incomparable and forces vendors to redo the same work for every customer. Standardized questionnaires fix both problems by giving everyone a shared, reusable format.

questions.q: What does CAIQ, published by the Cloud Security Alliance, map directly to?
options: The CSA's Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM), so a "yes" answer corresponds to a specific, published control
A vendor's internal org chart
The ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability of the customer, not the vendor
The customer's own internal risk register
questions.explain: CAIQ questions map directly to the Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM), so an answer corresponds to a specific, named control in a published framework rather than just the vendor's own wording.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the single most common and most expensive mistake in vendor risk management?
options: Using SIG instead of CAIQ for a cloud vendor
Asking vendors for a SOC 2 report at all
Treating every vendor identically instead of tiering assessment depth to actual risk
Allowing a vendor to complete a questionnaire electronically instead of on paper
questions.explain: Running the same full-depth review for a low-risk vendor and a high-risk vendor wastes limited GRC resources on vendors that don't need it while under-scrutinizing the vendors that actually matter.

questions.q: Which two factors does this lesson say should be combined to tier a vendor's assessment depth?
options: The vendor's annual revenue and number of employees
Whether the vendor's logo appears on its own marketing website
How long the vendor has existed and its headquarters location
Data sensitivity and access level
questions.explain: Tiering combines data sensitivity (does the vendor touch regulated or confidential data) and access level (network, system, or physical access versus none) to determine how deep an assessment needs to be.

questions.q: Why does a mature assessment process ask for independent evidence, such as a SOC 2 Type II report, instead of relying only on questionnaire answers?
options: Because questionnaires are illegal to use for vendor assessment under most frameworks
Because a SOC 2 report replaces the need for any questionnaire entirely
Because a questionnaire response is a self-attestation, and independent evidence corroborates whether the vendor's own answers are actually true
Because SOC 2 reports are the only acceptable evidence under CAIQ
questions.explain: A questionnaire is the vendor grading its own homework. Independent evidence like a SOC 2 Type II report, an ISO 27001 certificate, or a pen test summary corroborates whether the self-reported answers hold up.
